title: U.S. Senate · Kentucky

context.text: This is an open-seat race. Incumbent Mitch McConnell (R), who has held the seat since 1985, announced on February 20, 2025 that he would not seek re-election in 2026.

U.S. Representative Andy Barr (R, KY-6) won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 60.5% of the vote, defeating Daniel Cameron (30.8%) and nine other candidates. Charles Booker won the Democratic primary with 46.8% of the vote, defeating Amy McGrath (35.9%) and five other candidates.

candidates.name: Andy Barr
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 60.5% of the vote.

summary.text: Andy Barr is the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Kentucky and the U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 6th District, which he has held since 2013. A Lexington attorney by training, he worked in the Fletcher state administration before winning his House seat. He won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary over Daniel Cameron with 60.5% of the vote and describes himself as a conservative ally of President Trump.

background.text: Born in Lexington, Kentucky, in 1973; he is a graduate of Henry Clay High School in Lexington.
Received a B.A. in government and philosophy from the University of Virginia and a J.D. from the University of Kentucky College of Law in 2001.
Worked as a legislative assistant to Rep. Jim Talent (R-Mo.), then as an attorney, part-time law professor at Morehead State University, and deputy general counsel to Kentucky Gov. Ernie Fletcher.
Returned to private legal practice in 2008 and also taught constitutional law part-time at the University of Kentucky.
Lost his first House race in 2010 to Democratic Rep. Ben Chandler by about 650 votes (49.8% to 50.1%), then defeated Chandler in 2012 to win Kentucky's 6th District.
Took office in January 2013 and has been re-elected since, including a 51% to 48% win over Amy McGrath in 2018.

In the House, he serves on the Financial Services and Foreign Affairs committees and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, according to Ballotpedia.
According to his campaign website, he wrote a bill to block Biden administration ESG rules for retirement accounts that became the first veto of Joe Biden's presidency.
Announced on April 22, 2025 that he would run for the Senate seat being vacated by Mitch McConnell, and won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary over Daniel Cameron and others.
According to his campaign website, he lives in Lexington with his wife, Davis, and their four children.

priorities.text: "Andy Barr believes we must deport all criminal illegals and secure the border," citing his vote for a 2025 border security bill and support for restarting border wall construction, hiring more border agents, reinstating the Remain in Mexico policy, and ending catch and release.

Cutting taxes: "In 2025, he voted for the largest tax cut in American history, the Big Beautiful Bill," which his campaign says ended taxes on Social Security for seniors, overtime pay, and tips for Kentucky workers.

"Andy has a plan to bring back clean, beautiful coal, to create jobs, lower energy costs, and attract industries of the future to Kentucky," opposing what his campaign calls Biden-era ESG mandates and energy regulation.

positions.summary: Supports mass deportation of people in the country illegally who have committed crimes, voted to impeach the Biden administration's DHS secretary, and campaigns on restarting border wall construction and ending catch-and-release policies.
positions.quote: Andy Barr believes we must deport all criminal illegals and secure the border.

positions.summary: Opposes raising taxes and campaigns on having voted for the 2025 reconciliation tax-cut law ("Big Beautiful Bill"), contrasting his position with his opponent's on taxes.
positions.quote: Charles Booker will raise taxes on every Kentuckian, Andy Barr wants to cut taxes for every Kentuckian.

positions.summary: Campaigns against restrictions on fossil fuels, supporting expanded coal production and opposing environmental, social and governance (ESG) energy mandates.

candidates.name: Charles Booker
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 46.8% of the vote.

summary.text: Charles Booker is the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Kentucky. A Louisville native and former state representative, he ran for the Senate in 2020 (losing the Democratic primary) and in 2022 (losing the general election to Rand Paul). He won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 46.8% of the vote and campaigns on health care, jobs and fighting poverty.

background.text: Grew up in Louisville's West End and describes himself as a lifelong Kentuckian; says he experienced poverty and homelessness and has Type 1 diabetes.
Earned a B.S. in political science (2007) and a J.D. (2010) from the University of Louisville; says he was the first in his family to graduate from college and law school.

Worked as an education and equity policy analyst with the Louisville Urban League, manager of neighborhood initiatives with the Louisville Independent Business Alliance, division director of administrative services with the Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources, and director of development of 1619 Flux.

Served in the Kentucky House of Representatives (District 43) from January 2019 to December 2020 and did not seek re-election in 2020. His House committees included Natural Resources and Energy and Judiciary.
According to his campaign website, he helped lead the effort behind Breonna's Law while in the House.
Ran in the 2020 Democratic U.S. Senate primary, losing to Amy McGrath 45.4% to 42.6%. Afterward he founded Hood to the Holler, a grassroots organization, according to his Ballotpedia survey.
Was the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in 2022, losing to Rand Paul 61.8% to 38.2%.
Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 46.8%, ahead of Amy McGrath (35.9%). According to his campaign website, he is the father of two daughters.

priorities.text: "Kentucky deserves a senator who fights poverty like the emergency it is ... This campaign is about ... Healthcare as a human right. Union jobs in every county. Clean water and clean air."

positions.summary: Campaigns on making healthcare a human right, citing his own experience rationing insulin growing up.

As a Kentucky state representative, voted no on HB 5, which restricted abortions performed because of the sex, race, or a disability diagnosis of the fetus and declared an emergency; the House passed it 67-25.

record.text: Voted no on HB 5 (restricting abortion performed because of the sex, race, or a disability diagnosis of the fetus), which passed the Kentucky House 67-25 on February 26, 2019.
Voted no on the final-passage appropriation for SB 2 (requiring voters to present photo identification), which passed the Kentucky House 58-25 on March 19, 2020.
Was primary sponsor of HB 6 in the 2020 session, a proposed constitutional amendment to restore voting rights for people convicted of felonies after completion of their sentence.

summary.text: Christopher Campbell is the Kentucky Party candidate for U.S. Senate, a health care worker from Marion County who served in the Army National Guard. He says he supports a Medicare for All-style system and reducing U.S. military spending abroad.

background.text: Says he has lived in Kentucky his whole life and grew up in Marion County.
Says he is a graduate of Kentucky's public school system and Eastern Kentucky University; Ballotpedia lists a graduate degree from Eastern Kentucky University in 2019.
Served in the U.S. Army National Guard from 2013 to 2019, according to Ballotpedia.

Says he has worked in health care, including in nursing homes, hospitals, health departments and rape crisis centers; Ballotpedia lists his career experience as including work as an independent contractor.

priorities.text: "Healthcare is a basic human right...especially, when we live in the wealthiest nation on Earth ... a Medicare For All plan will save U.S. taxpayers several trillions of dollars."
Says he would push for a moratorium on foreign military aid, consolidation of overseas U.S. military bases, and a ban on defense-contractor lobbying of Congress.

positions.summary: Supports a Medicare for All-style public healthcare system.
positions.quote: Healthcare is a basic human right...especially, when we live in the wealthiest nation on Earth.

positions.summary: Supports a moratorium on U.S. military aid to foreign governments generally, as part of opposing what he calls the "Military-Industrial Complex."

summary.text: Thomas Murphy is an independent write-in candidate for U.S. Senate in Kentucky, campaigning as 'BRAVE 2026 - Murphy for Kentucky.' No biographical profile of his education, career or prior offices was found.

background.text: His campaign website, titled 'BRAVE 2026 - Murphy for Kentucky,' says 'Parties are the Problem' and directs voters to write in his name for U.S. Senate; it gives no biographical details.
